races.name: Scullion Law 'Law Firm For Life' Ebf Maiden Stakes (gbb Race)
Strathmore Hotels Ltd Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)
Pdm Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Cabrera
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Edward Bethell with P.J. McDonald up; recent form shows out-of-the-frame finishes over 12f on Good, but the step up to 1m5f looks a natural progression, and solo pace-setting on this flat Hamilton track could prove decisive if rivals fail to close.

runners_data.name: High Point
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 5yo has won and placed over 16f on Soft and Standard, suggesting stamina is a genuine asset at this trip; hold-up style suits a strongly-run race but sim-going record of 0W0P on Good is a concern, and 51 days off means fitness must be respected.

runners_data.name: Secret Force
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley-trained 4yo boasts three wins on Good ground including over 17f and 18f, making the trip and conditions an excellent fit; prominent style means he should be able to track Cabrera and challenge turning in, and T14 strike rate of 4/19 shows the yard is firing.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's 4yo has placed in five of six starts on Good, evidencing consistency at this level, though it wears a hood and has finished no better than 2nd in recent starts; prominent style suits this shape but the win has been elusive and OR of 73 leaves little room for error.

runners_data.name: Dunkeld Dreamer
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced 3yo for K.R. Burke with a win over 12f on Good and placed efforts over 9-13f, showing clear improvement on this surface; sits on the right side of prominent runners to benefit from tracking Cabrera, though conceding weight as a 3yo and stepping to 1m5f first time are genuine questions.

runners_data.name: Ouro Preto
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's 5yo has a deeply uninspiring recent form string of 7-9-9-7-11 and a sim-going record of 0W0P on Good; hold-up style is unlikely to be rewarded in what should be a steadily-run race.

runners_data.name: Eroico
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's 4yo is a genuine hold-up horse by nature but is pushed into midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed; has placed twice over this sort of trip on Good, though a true late run demands stronger pace than Cabrera alone is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Spanish Hustle
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's veteran 8yo wears a hood and shows a form string of 8-0-0-6-6, with no win from 11 recent Good-ground starts; hold-up profile is deeply unsuited to the expected controlled tempo at 1m5f.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's 7yo has won over 15-16f on Soft and Good, giving him a genuine staying profile, but his true hold-up style is redistributed to midfield here because rear positions are crowded; the trip suits well and a recent 3rd on Good encourages, but getting into the race from a non-natural position is the challenge.

runners_data.name: Cotton Bud
runners_data.note: Shaun Lycett's 3yo is a natural prominent racer by style but the field depth forces her back toward midfield in practice; won on Good over 10f and has placed over 8f, so stamina at 1m5f is an open question, and 79 days off for a lightly-raced 3yo adds further risk.

runners_data.name: Wootton's Gal
runners_data.note: Richard & Peter Fahey's 3yo has placed over 11-12f on Good but the form figures of 5-2-4 show more ability than wins, and being a true hold-up type pushed out of her natural rearward position means getting competitive is harder; 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall (5) keeps the weight down but experience is limited.

races.paceDynamic: Cabrera is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Secret Force, Gentle Warrior, and Dunkeld Dreamer as genuine prominent types to apply any pressure, the pace in this 1m5f Hamilton handicap is likely to be measured and sustainable rather than frantic. Cabrera will dictate from the front at a controlled tempo on Good ground, with Secret Force and Dunkeld Dreamer likely to sit just behind, meaning the race will be run at an honest but not punishing gallop. The field contains more pace than can be naturallyaccommodated — Cotton Bud is a true prominent type who will be squeezed toward midfield, while Eroico, Gallus Norman, and Wootton's Gal are genuine hold-up horses pushed into the midfield zone on the map because the rear is oversubscribed. Given one front-runner controlling a moderate tempo over a staying trip on fast-ish Good ground at Hamilton, this race shape most heavily favours prominent racers who can sit just off the pace and pounce in the straight, with true hold-up horses likely to face a difficult task if the pace is not strong enough to set them alight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cabrera Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cabrera sets a controlled solo pace and prominent rivals Secret Force or Dunkeld Dreamer track closely before striking turning for home.
scenarios.body: Cabrera's uncontested lead produces a measured pace that keeps the race together until the final two furlongs, rewarding horses who have travelled prominently without burning energy early. Secret Force's strong Good-ground form at this sort of trip and Dunkeld Dreamer's consistent placing record over 12-13f both suit this shape ideally.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Cabrera Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves slow enough that Cabrera's stamina advantage turns the race into a test of attrition from the front.
scenarios.body: Cabrera controls every yard, the moderate fractions favour the leader as rivals fail to accelerate late, and the field strings out in the straight with no one able to get on terms. This is a realistic outcome given Cabrera is a confirmed front-runner facing only gentle pressure, though its recent out-of-the-frame finishes over 12f suggest the step to 13f+ is needed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough — perhaps with Secret Force pushing Cabrera — to set up a late run for the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A truly run race over this stamina trip could allow Gallus Norman or High Point, both of whom have course-distance form, to finish with purpose through beaten horses. However, this scenario is discounted because multiple hold-up horses (Eroico, Gallus Norman, Wootton's Gal) are mapped out of their natural rear positions, meaning few true closers will be able to get into the race at their preferred late stage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses contest the early lead more aggressively than expected and the pace fractures.
scenarios.body: Cotton Bud, a genuine prominent type squeezed toward midfield, might press forward if the pace is slow, creating a contested lead that burns out Cabrera and opens the race for a midfield mover. This is the least likely shape given the clear pace hierarchy, but Cotton Bud's win on Good ground over shorter trips hints at untapped bold-front ambitions.

watchPoints.text: Cabrera's solo lead could be entirely uncontested — if P.J. McDonald sets even a modest pace, Secret Force and Dunkeld Dreamer must be tracked from the start to see if either applies pressure before the home turn.

Cotton Bud is a genuine prominent type squeezed into midfield — watch the early stages to see if Gina Mangan pushes forward aggressively, which could turn a controlled race into a contested pace and fundamentally alter the race shape.

Gallus Norman has strong staying form over 15-16f on Good and could be the biggest beneficiary if the pace is genuinely strong, but Paul Mulrennan will need to find a clean passage from a non-natural midfield starting point.

Hamilton's flat 1m5f trip historically favours prominent racers over closers — any hold-up horse requiring a truly strong pace to deliver its run faces a structural disadvantage here regardless of form.

K.R. Burke saddles two runners (Gentle Warrior and Dunkeld Dreamer) who could tactically influence each other — monitor which jockey takes the more forward position, as this shapes the pressure on Cabrera from multiple angles.

races.name: Cube Glass 'soba' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Corolla Point
runners_data.note: Won twice at 5f on good going and arrives here as the lone confirmed pace-setter; P-style horse gets to roll from the front without a direct challenger, making this a standout tactical opportunity, though its OR of 97 means it carries a penalty that the field will target.

runners_data.name: Purosangue
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Robert Cowell but a flat zero wins or places from 15 runs on comparable going — the form figures simply do not inspire confidence at this trip on this surface regardless of where it settles.

runners_data.name: Arklow Lad
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's gelding has three wins from 11 on soft-comparable going and carries the tongue-tie, returning after 56 days which is worth monitoring; naturally prominent and drops into a race where the front positions are genuinely contestable.

runners_data.name: Another Baar
runners_data.note: The form string of 100060 across good and soft ground spells out a horse in poor current form; tongue-tie fitted but six runs without troubling the judge on similar going makes this hard to enthuse about tactically.

runners_data.name: Manila Scouse
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old has excellent course-and-distance exposure and two wins on good going from 15 similar starts; sits naturally prominent and has the weight advantage to press Corolla Point without fully committing to front-running duties.

runners_data.name: Eternal Sunshine
runners_data.note: Strong recent run (2nd, 7 days ago) shows sharp fitness for Jim Goldie, and this is a genuine prominent racer by nature — however, with several others wanting the same berth, it will likely find itself racing slightly further back than ideal, which constrains its winning chances.

runners_data.name: Venture Capital
runners_data.note: Returning from 108 days off for Kevin Ryan, which is the longest absence in this field; a true hold-up type whose last win on good ground came as recently as 5f, but the lengthy lay-off and poor recent figures (8-7-8) demand caution — sits in mapped midfield not entirely by choice.

runners_data.name: Fivethousandtoone
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old handicapper for Tim Easterby who naturally wants to race prominently but the crowded front end in this 14-runner field will squeeze him back; two placed efforts at 6f on this track suggest course familiarity, but being denied his preferred position is a real cost.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on good going and was placed twice on soft, so the ground is fine; Iain Jardine's seven-year-old is a natural front-prominent type who won most recently when able to race close to the pace — being unable to secure that berth today is the central risk to its chances.

runners_data.name: Solar Aclaim
runners_data.note: Julie Camacho's five-year-old has a solitary win on soft at 5f and a sequence of poor finishes on good; OR 91 but form figures do not match that rating recently, and as a genuine hold-up type this trip gives it minimal room to produce a telling late move.

runners_data.name: Fluorescence
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's four-year-old has placed four times from ten on comparable going but showed an unseated-rider last time — the form before that includes a 4th at 5f on soft, and as a naturally prominent-style runner the front positions here are legitimately available to it.

runners_data.name: Vantheman
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's five-year-old has ten course runs and a win at 5f on good, fitting the Hamilton profile well; the blue blinkers focus its prominent racing style and 15 days since a last run suggests freshness — one of the better-placed prominent types to challenge if Corolla Point is pressured.

runners_data.name: Jordan Electrics
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's ten-year-old was beaten a neck into 3rd at 6f on good last time and 1st at 6f on good the run before — genuine course and going form, races from hold-up to midfield naturally, and Paul Mulrennan knows this horse well; dropping to 5f may test stamina in reverse but the finishing form is live.

runners_data.name: Canon's House
runners_data.note: Michael & David Easterby's five-year-old placed at 5f on good and soft and has course experience; sits naturally prominent and with three trainer winners over 14 days that yard is in decent order — a solid each-way profile if the pace is honest.

races.paceDynamic: Corolla Point is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with one pacemaker among 14 runners, will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — Hamilton's stiff 5f finish means a sensible pace here is not necessarily a slow one, but this horse will not be pressured into setting a frantic tempo. Manila Scouse, Arklow Lad, Vantheman, Fluorescence and Canon's House will all push forward to race prominently and are genuine rivals for the front rank; several will sit just off Corolla Point's shoulder rather than challenge for the lead itself. The field contains more prominent-type runners than the shape can accommodate: Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone and Parisiac are all natural prominent racers who will be shuffled back into a midfield role against their preferred style, which materially reduces their chance in any scenario that demands they are up close early. The tactical verdict is clear: with a lone front-runner controlling an honest but uncontested pace and several rivals forced to race out of position, horses that can sit naturally prominent or work into contention from a genuine midfield berth — rather than those who need to be on the pace but can't get there — are best served by this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Corolla Point Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Corolla Point gets a clean break and settles into an uncontested rhythm that the prominent pack cannot close down on Hamilton's stiff finish.
scenarios.body: Corolla Point dictates from the front without a pace rival breathing down its neck, and the honest but sustainable gallop plays to the fitness of horses dropping down in class or carrying lower weight off the front; Hamilton's uphill finish rewards those who have conserved energy rather than chased hard in the early stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trio Overwhelm Lone Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the leaders push on hard enough that Corolla Point is pressed into a faster pace, leaving the prominent pack to run past a weakening leader in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Manila Scouse, Arklow Lad and Vantheman press Corolla Point hard enough to force a genuine gallop that undermines the leader's stamina reserves; the first quarter of Hamilton's 5f is marginally downhill before the stiff climb home, and horses with good course form or class advantages at this trip can pick up as the leader flattens.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Finish Fast
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to string out the field and allow horses settled in true midfield to pick off a tiring front group in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Jordan Electrics or Canon's House, racing from a genuine midfield position with strong recent form, finds the split as the prominent group races itself into the ground; the key is that Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone and Parisiac — natural prominent types displaced to midfield — do not truly settle or produce a natural late run, limiting the depth of the closing surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is uncharacteristically strong and Hamilton's finish is churned out faster than typical, leaving a genuine late-runner to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Purosangue or Solar Aclaim, sitting furthest back, needs an unusually hot pace to have enough weakening horses to pass in the final furlong on what is a short-enough trip to make a closing run very difficult; this scenario is the least likely given the sole front-runner and the compressed midfield that will limit the gap between sections.

watchPoints.text: Corolla Point's ability to stride clear unchallenged in the opening furlong is the single biggest factor — watch whether Manila Scouse or Arklow Lad pushes up to press it immediately off the stalls, which would fundamentally change the tempo dynamic.

Eternal Sunshine, Fivethousandtoone and Parisiac all want to race prominently but cannot all get there — watch the early scramble for position on the inside because crowding or interference in the first two furlongs could compromise multiple runners simultaneously.

Venture Capital returns from 108 days off and is the most significant fitness unknown in the field; if Shane Gray is forced to push the horse up earlier than planned to find a clear run, its stamina may not hold to the stiff finish.

Jordan Electrics brings the best recent form of the hold-up types — back-to-back placed runs at 6f on good — and Paul Mulrennan's record at Hamilton merits noting; it will need Corolla Point to fade sharply on the climb to the line but is worth tracking from the 2f pole.

Hamilton's 5f is entirely flat in profile but the finish is legitimately stiff — watch the sectionals from the 2f marker, as any front-runner still travelling at that point tends to hold on, while closers who haven't closed by then rarely do.

races.name: Blitz Cleaning Commercial Cleaning Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hundred Caps
runners_data.note: Consistent sort who has finished second or better three times in six starts and goes on good ground — Sam James retains the ride and Julie Camacho has low recent strike rate (0/16 in 14 days), but Hundred Caps' natural forcing style means the low trainer form matters less here than for a hold-up type.

runners_data.name: Stirrup Cup
runners_data.note: Returned a 45-day break after back-to-back good-ground efforts and has course-distance form, but races from hold-up position and Hamilton's sharp five furlongs rarely rewards horses who need to make up significant late ground.

runners_data.name: Tiriac
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a poor recent sequence — 9, 8, 7, 17 in last four — and no wins or placed efforts on good going in this sample; Paul Midgley yard is quiet (1/19 in 14 days) and there is little to encourage at this point.

runners_data.name: King's Crown
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves takes over on this six-year-old who has placed at shorter trip on good ground (3rd at 5f on soft) but lacks a win in some time; hold-up style means he needs the race to fall apart in front of him, which is a lower-probability outcome today.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Amie Waugh claims 3lbs for this seven-year-old who won last time at 5f on good — a genuinely positive angle — but Harb's natural style is hold-up and this horse has been redistributed into a midfield position it would not naturally occupy; the real running style should be discounted against a race likely run at a moderate clip.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Consistent on good ground with four places from six attempts at 5f, Lauren Young claims 5lbs, and this prominent runner is exactly the profile that suits a steady-tempo Hamilton sprint — four successive placed efforts show she rarely runs a bad race.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine has two runners in this race and Mount Ruapehu is the stablemate, freshened after 12 days; consistently finishes in mid-division and the six-year-old's OR of 59 is the third-lowest in the field, which limits upside even in a race it can sit prominently.

runners_data.name: Never Dark
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran, naturally a hold-up horse who has been mapped into midfield due to field compression — aged profile and recent 6-6-7-8-3 sequence in good-going sprints suggests the back end of the field is a ceiling rather than a launchpad; Gina Mangan partnership has limited recent form together.

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi
runners_data.note: Andrew Mullen rides this in-form five-year-old who has won twice in last six and goes well on good ground (1-2 in similar conditions) — prominent racing style suits today's pace dynamic well, and a low OR of 70 means any weight-advantage over rivals is meaningful.

runners_data.name: Oriental Prince
runners_data.note: Paul Mulrennan takes the mount on this five-year-old who has run 5th, 4th, 7th, 20th, 8th in last five — the 20-length Goodwood defeat flatters to deceive and the hold-up style combined with a flat recent sequence offers little tactical purchase in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: High-class recent form (1-2-1-1-3 in last six) and Kaiya Fraser rides — this eight-year-old holds the strongest raw form in the field but is a true hold-up horse pressed into midfield by the volume of closers in this race; the genuine ability is there, though racing out of preferred position at 5f on a track that suits prominent horses tempers the outlook.

runners_data.name: Jm Jhingree
runners_data.note: Greg Fairley partners this four-year-old who won two runs ago over 5f on good (OR 66 is fair) and has a visor fitted — a natural hold-up runner pushed toward midfield by field compression, so the headgear could sharpen early engagement but the redistribution means Ewan Whillans' yard (3/9 in 14 days, solid) counts for less than it might.

races.paceDynamic: Hundred Caps is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should slot comfortably into a position just off the pace or on the front end at a sustainable gallop on good ground at Hamilton. Thunderstorm Katie and Mount Ruapehu will push to race prominently behind, while Little Mi Mi is another who likes to be up with the pace — these three will contest the chasing positions and ensure a sensibly-run rather than truly dawdling tempo. The field carries a substantial cluster of hold-up horses (Iris Dancer, Jm Jhingree, Harb, Never Dark) who cannot all get their natural position at the back and will be forced closer to the pace than ideal, effectively compressing the field. With a single, uncontested pace-setter on good ground over five furlongs, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Hundred Caps and sprint from a close-up position, as the lack of a truly fierce pace reduces the chance of closers arriving late with a decisive run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent stalker pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hundred Caps sets a controlled, unhurried tempo and the race is decided by those immediately tracking from a handy position.
scenarios.body: Hundred Caps rolls along in front without pressure, and the horses positioned just behind — Thunderstorm Katie, Little Mi Mi — are ideally placed to sprint past as the hill bites in the final furlong; good ground suits runners who sustain their effort rather than those needing a fast pace to close into.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner holds on
scenarios.trigger: If Hundred Caps is allowed to dictate an even, unchallenged pace and the field fails to close on the run-in.
scenarios.body: With no horse willing or able to apply sustained early pressure, Hundred Caps could simply ping along at its own rhythm and prove too far ahead to catch; Hamilton's five furlongs on good ground does not always produce dramatic late swoops when the pace has been fair rather than fierce.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse cuts through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses into a crawl in the first two furlongs and a genuine finisher threads through a compressed field late.
scenarios.body: Iris Dancer and Jm Jhingree carry the best hold-up credentials in the field and have the form — particularly Iris Dancer's recent 1-2-1 sequence — to finish powerfully if a true sprint finish develops; however, both are tagged as redistributed out of their natural rear position, materially reducing the likelihood they can generate the angle they need.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses, chaos finish
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses push early and the pace proves too hot, causing front-end weakening across the board.
scenarios.body: Hundred Caps, Thunderstorm Katie and Mount Ruapehu could burn each other out in the first half of the race, opening the door for a hold-up horse that manages to find clear running late; Stirrup Cup and King's Crown, who race from further back, would be the natural beneficiaries of widespread front-end capitulation.

watchPoints.text: Thunderstorm Katie's four consecutive placed efforts on good ground and prominent racing style make her the primary threat to capitalise if Hundred Caps sets a fair, uncontested tempo — watch how quickly Lauren Young has her settled behind the leader.

Little Mi Mi won two of her last six and races prominently — Andrew Mullen will aim to track Hundred Caps and could easily be the one who swoops at the top of the hill; her stable (Iain Jardine) saddles three runners in the race, so watch for pace orders between stablemates.

Iris Dancer's 1-2-1-1-3 recent form is significantly the best in the field — if Kaiya Fraser secures a closer position than natural and gets a clear run in the final furlong, the raw ability could overcome the positional disadvantage; the style mismatch is a concern but not a disqualifier.

Hundred Caps has no pacefoe to pressure it and Camacho/James partnership may aim to dictate from in front rather than race off the pace — if Hundred Caps leads rather than chases, the race shape simplifies considerably and Scenario B becomes live.

The Iain Jardine trio (Mount Ruapehu, Never Dark, Little Mi Mi) creates stable-order uncertainty — if Little Mi Mi is the preferred runner, the stablemates may be ridden conservatively, which could affect pace dynamics in the chasing group.

races.name: Gss Contracts Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rajapour
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer for David O'Meara, back quickly after just 7 days; has won and placed on good ground at this 8f trip (1W4P in similar going) but needs a true pace collapse to get involved from the rear, wearing tongue strap and hood.

runners_data.name: Intrusively
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old is a consistent hold-up type who has placed at 10f and 8f on good, but OR 75 form shows a pattern of hitting the frame without winning; the lack of any pace-setter to chase may blunt this horse's finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Sunriseontheboyne
runners_data.note: Ben Haslam runner returning after 60 days off, which is notable; hold-up style on a horse whose best distance form suggests 8f rather than longer, and the Hamilton 1m½f trip on good ground represents an uncertain profile given limited comparable history.

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Richard and Peter Fahey's progressive four-year-old has won three of his last five including back-to-back on good ground, racing from a natural prominent position — best-placed in the field to attach himself to Sanafi Zabeel's pace and strike from the front rank.

runners_data.name: Midsummer Storm
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke three-year-old with a genuine hold-up profile being mapped to midfield; the horse has only raced four times with zero wins or places, and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 reflects that racing away from its natural late position materially weakens its claims here.

runners_data.name: Sanafi Zabeel
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's five-year-old is the race's sole front-runner with a clear remit to lead; Paul Mulrennan can set a controlled tempo from the front, and five of six runs on good ground with 1W4P in similar conditions underpin the merit of this position.

runners_data.name: Watcha Snoop
runners_data.note: Adam Nicol's three-year-old carries a finishing-fade flag and a deeply uninspiring form string of 0-0000, and its true hold-up style being displaced into midfield by the overcrowded rear profile gives almost no realistic route to the winner's enclosure.

runners_data.name: Starliner
runners_data.note: Linda Perratt's five-year-old shows back-to-back placings (2nd, 2nd) on good ground at 8f, giving it the best recent form of the redistributed closers; though a natural hold-up type asked to race in midfield, the in-form trainer angle (4/9 T14) is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Ephron
runners_data.note: Gemma Tutty's three-year-old has won at 8f on good ground and placed at 9f, but tends to race as a genuine closer; shuffled into midfield by the hold-up glut, the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 suggests this runner would much prefer a stronger pace to chase down.

runners_data.name: Yaaser
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's eight-year-old veteran has been running consistently in the 3-7 range at 7f on good ground but steps up in trip here; OR 58 is the field's lowest, the horse is a natural hold-up type placed into midfield by the race's demographic, and age-related limitations further temper its prospects.

races.paceDynamic: Sanafi Zabeel is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival for the lead, Paul Mulrennan can dictate a measured, uncontested gallop from the front over this 1m½f trip on good ground at Hamilton. The pace will be honest but controlled — Sanafi Zabeel's recent form shows consistent prominence and five of six runs on similar going, giving him a solid platform to roll along without being pressured into burning too much early. The remainder of the field is almost entirely hold-up or midfield in profile, meaning the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set it up for closers in the conventional sense — the horse in front gets to conserve energy and dictate terms. This race shape heavily favours a front-runner who can control fractions and a prominent racer with the tactical speed to attach themselves to Sanafi Zabeel early; Mwafaq is the most natural candidate to sit close to the pace from a genuine prominent style. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate — Midsummer Storm, Watcha Snoop, Starliner, Ephron, and Yaaser are all true closers who are unlikely to be racing in their preferred positions given the pedestrian pace on offer, with Mwafaq and potentially Rajapour best-placed to exploit their true roles.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sanafi Zabeel Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Sanafi Zabeel leads comfortably and the slow-to-moderate pace is never seriously challenged by the midfield pack.
scenarios.body: Mulrennan sets a sustainable tempo, the hold-up horses are stranded mid-pack with no pace injection to chase, and Sanafi Zabeel's strong good-ground record (5/6) sees him last home from a comfortable lead.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mwafaq Tracks And Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Mwafaq sits prominently just behind Sanafi Zabeel and produces a sustained run from two furlongs out to wear down the leader.
scenarios.body: Mwafaq's excellent recent form — three wins in last five runs including two on good ground — suits this prominent-attack shape perfectly, and the 5lb claimer Ethan Tindall keeps the weight burden manageable.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Gets Lucky Trip
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Sanafi Zabeel fades sharply inside the final furlong, gifting the closers a run they wouldn't naturally manufacture.
scenarios.body: Rajapour is the most likely beneficiary as the highest-rated hold-up type with a win on good ground at this trip, though the redistribution of so many true closers into midfield means the closer-laden bunch will be fighting each other for the same late ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Starliner
scenarios.trigger: If the even gallop and Hamilton's unique undulations allow one of the midfield types who genuinely acts on this track to grind out a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Starliner has placed twice in recent good-ground runs at 8f and trainer Linda Perratt has a 4/9 14-day strike rate suggesting a horse in form, though the redistribution from natural hold-up to midfield map position tempers confidence in this shape materialising.

watchPoints.text: Sanafi Zabeel (Paul Mulrennan) — watch whether he is allowed a completely uncontested lead from the gates; if anything forces him wider or a rival jumps with him, the dynamics of his dictation change materially.

Mwafaq (Ethan Tindall, 5lb claim) — watch the early positioning; if the claimer can slot Mwafaq into second or third behind Sanafi Zabeel within the first two furlongs, that prominent berth becomes the single most dangerous tactical position in the race.

Rajapour — returning after just 7 days, watch whether Mark Winn drops him in at the rear as normal or attempts to creep closer given the lack of genuine pace; if he misses the break or is stuck wide, even a pace collapse may not bring him into the picture.

Starliner — watch for a prominent move from Linda Perratt's runner despite the midfield mapping; back-to-back seconds on good ground suggest this horse is race-fit and may travel better than its OR 63 suggests, making it a potential each-way outsider if it gets a clean passage.

Watcha Snoop — flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, watch whether Shane Gray attempts to race more prominently than the form suggests to avoid the fade; any early boldness would be telling but should not be trusted to be maintained.

races.name: Wellman Cars Hamilton Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Braes Of Doune
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old who has placed twice in seven Good-ground starts at this trip; Paul Mulrennan knows this horse well, and tracking Pisanello from a prominent pitch is his natural game — the 19-day break is manageable and Jim Goldie has a respectable 2/37 14-day record.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has won twice recently on Good ground over this distance; the 3-day turnaround is a stamina flag, headgear (v) suggests he needs freshening, and STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 is only a concern if he is forced to race off his natural pace — here, he won't be.

runners_data.name: Hostelry
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Ruth Carr who has been consistently placed over 8f on Good but struggles to win; Tom Eaves will need a smooth passage from the rear in a field full of similar types, and the nine-year-old's 21-day absence is straightforward enough.

runners_data.name: Defence Missile
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a recent win to his name (AW) and showing improved form; Kaiya Fraser takes over for Linda Perratt who is in good 14-day form (4/9), though stepping up to 9f from recent 7-8f assignments is the key fitness question — the hold-up style is genuine but the draw and traffic may matter.

runners_data.name: Jenson Benson
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old whose true running style is rear-of-field, but the sheer volume of hold-up horses in this race means he cannot settle as far back as he'd like; the 291-day absence is a serious concern, and Shaun Lycett's 0/2 14-day record offers no confidence — best trip has been 10-12f, shorter here.

runners_data.name: Evelyn's Phoenix
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has been running over 8f on Good and Soft without landing a blow recently, and 48 days off plus a 0 last time out dampens enthusiasm; though a true hold-up type by nature, the compressed field shape means he will likely find himself in mid-division without clear daylight when it matters.

runners_data.name: Can I Kiss You
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who carries a ⚠ fade flag backed by a string of finishing positions in the 8-11 range; Andrew Mullen inherits a horse that is a genuine closer by inclination but is mapped to midfield given the field's hold-up glut — the late fade tendency makes this a long-shot to land the prize.

runners_data.name: Ring Of Gold
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old entire who has been winless on Good ground across 15 recorded runs in similar conditions; Lewis Chalkley (7) is an inexperienced claimer, and the horse's redistribution from his natural hold-up position in a rear-stacked field is an additional layer of difficulty on top of deteriorating form.

runners_data.name: Saxon Grace
runners_data.note: Three-year-old filly from Daragh Bourke's yard with no wins in six starts and a form string of 674640 that shows no progression; stepping up sharply in trip from 5-7f to 9f is untested, the trainer is 0/1 over 14 days, and while the low weight offers theoretical assistance, nothing in her profile screams for this race.

races.paceDynamic: Pisanello is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-horse field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate from the front at a sustainable gallop over this 1m1f trip on Good turf at Hamilton. Braes Of Doune is the likely closest pursuer from a prominent berth, but the remainder of the field — Hostelry, Defence Missile, Jenson Benson, Evelyn's Phoenix, Can I Kiss You, Ring Of Gold and Saxon Grace — are all hold-up types in a field that is heavily stacked toward the rear. The field holds more hold-up types than can all settle comfortably off the pace; Jenson Benson, Evelyn's Phoenix, Can I Kiss You and Ring Of Gold are redistributed to midfield on the map but are unlikely to secure their natural late-running position in a race where the pace is moderate and the pack may compress. A lone front-runner setting a controlled, uncontested tempo on Good ground over this trip strongly favours prominent racers who can track and pounce rather than hold-up horses trying to close from deep, as the lack of pressure up front will limit the ground those closers can make up in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pisanello Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Pisanello dictates a relaxed, uncontested pace and the hold-up pack lacks the sprint to reel him in off a slow gallop.
scenarios.body: Pisanello has won twice on Good ground over this trip and, given no pressure, can set fractions that suit his relaxed front-running style and produce a strong finish; Braes Of Doune, tracking in second throughout, is ideally placed to challenge or inherit the prize if Pisanello's recent 3-day turnaround blunts his finishing kick.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pisanello's pace proves just sustainable enough to stretch the field but Braes Of Doune or Hostelry tracks closely and outstays him in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A patient prominent runner stalking the front-runner through a controlled pace is well-positioned to benefit when the leader tires close home; Braes Of Doune's solid course-distance form on Good and Hostelry's consistent placing record make them the most credible challengers in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to open a gap for a closer, or a midfield racer gets an ideal run through on the rail in the straight.
scenarios.body: Defence Missile, who showed a win recently and has decent course form, could benefit if the pace fragments and creates a sprint from two furlongs out; Evelyn's Phoenix, despite being redistributed from a true hold-up role, has the speed rating to capitalise if the race sets up with a strong enough gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Pisanello is taken on unexpectedly or tires sharply, fragmenting the field and creating a cavalry charge finish.
scenarios.body: A scrambled finish from the home turn would compress the field and give redistributed runners like Jenson Benson or Ring Of Gold a chance to grab an unlikely placing, though their true hold-up styles and modest recent form make this a low-probability outcome; Saxon Grace, carrying the lowest weight as a three-year-old, is the wildcard who could benefit from a truly messy pace scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch Pisanello's early jump and whether Conor Whiteley elects to dictate immediately — if anything presses him for the lead in the first furlong, the pace dynamic shifts entirely and the prominent/midfield pack could be in business.
Jenson Benson's 291-day absence is a significant fitness concern; if he tires sharply in the straight he could cause interference for the hold-up horses trying to run through on his outside.

The redistribution of four hold-up types — Jenson Benson, Evelyn's Phoenix, Can I Kiss You and Ring Of Gold — into midfield means traffic will be dense in the pack; watch for a wall of horses through the final two furlongs with limited room to manoeuvre.

Defence Missile is the youngest horse in the field at four and is stepping up in trip; monitor early whether Kaiya Fraser settles him immediately off the pace or whether he attempts to race more prominently than his official hold-up tag suggests.

Saxon Grace (3yo) carries 13lb less than the top weights — if the race develops into a sprint off a slow early pace, watch whether the filly's youth and weight allowance translate into any unexpected late momentum.
